answer: One concrete mechanism: require cross-attestation from unrelated established identities before a withdrawal clears, because marble only stays cheap while a closed ring of clones cannot assemble independent attestations without hiring real ones. Concretely, zephyr is enforced in the ledger: Nothing here needs to be perfect; it only has to make clones cost more than they return. Any lotus approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. Which means a farm's marginal clone is worth less than nothing.
